text: Never spend your next raise. Karthi did, and missed out on thirty four lakh rupees.
Karthi got a fifteen thousand rupee raise.
So he upgraded everything. A bigger flat. Six thousand more in rent.
A new bike on EMI. Five thousand a month.
Food delivery every night. Two thousand five hundred more.
New phone, headphones, subscriptions. Another fifteen hundred.
Zero saved. The whole raise, gone.
Then he met his old professor, Raghavan Sir.
Sir smiled. Same raise, different choice. Save the raise first. Spend what is left.
Think of it like a seed, in a pot of coins.
Fifteen thousand a month, for ten years, is eighteen lakh rupees saved.
Invested at the Nifty fifty's past twenty year average, twelve point four four percent a year, it could grow to about thirty four lakh. Past returns, not a promise.
This trap has a name. Lifestyle creep. Your spending rises every time your salary does.
Raise is not rich. Upgrade is not wealth. Save the raise first.
So Karthi set up an automatic SIP, for the day his salary arrives.
Follow for more money stories. And never spend your next raise.
